content.text: Confirmed. Here's the bug: **The landing page (`/`) never redirects anywhere after login, and it doesn't check auth state at all.** - Your "Sign in" / "Get started" buttons both just link to `/auth/login` with no `returnTo` param (`src/app/page.tsx:16,28`). - The Auth0 SDK (`@auth0/nextjs-auth0` v4) processes `/auth/login` → Auth0 Universal Login → `/auth/callback` via the middleware in `src/proxy.ts`, and when no `returnTo` was specified, it lands you back on `/` by default. - `src/app/page.tsx` is a plain static landing page — it never calls `auth0.getSession()`, so it renders identically whether you're logged in or not. You end up back on `http://localhost:3000/` looking at the exact same "Sign in" button, which looks like sign-in silently did nothing. - The actual authenticated app lives under the `(app)` route group (`/today`, `/pantry`, etc.), guarded by `src/app/(app)/layout.tsx`, which does call `requireUser()` — but nothing sends you there after login. So it's not failing — you *are* signed in, you're just stranded on a landing page that doesn't know or care that you're signed in. **Fix:** point the sign-in links at `/today` as the return destination, e.g.: ```tsx Get started ``` (`@auth0/nextjs-auth0` v4's `/auth/login` route accepts a `returnTo` query param.) Optionally, also make `page.tsx` check `auth0.getSession()` and show a "Go to app" link / redirect when already signed in, so a signed-in user hitting `/` isn't stuck looking at the marketing page either. - The `were.cooking` block only serves `/`, `/_next/*`, `/favicon.ico` directly (the `@landing` matcher). Everything else — including `/auth/login` and `/auth/callback` — falls through to its `handle {}` block, which does `redir https://now.were.cooking{uri}`. So any auth request that hits `were.cooking` gets 302'd straight to `now.were.cooking` before it ever reaches the Next.js app.
- The `now.were.cooking` block only redirects the exact path `/` (either to `were.cooking` if logged out, or to `/today` if logged in); `/auth/login` and `/auth/callback` don't match either `redir`, so they pass straight through via `import app` to the Next.js container.

So the OAuth round-trip always actually completes on `now.were.cooking`. That means:
- `APP_BASE_URL=https://now.were.cooking` — this is what `@auth0/nextjs-auth0` uses to build the `redirect_uri` it sends to Auth0.
- Auth0 dashboard **Allowed Callback URLs** must include `https://now.were.cooking/auth/callback` to match.
- `were.cooking` only needs to appear in **Allowed Logout URLs** (since logout can send you back to the marketing page) and doesn't need to be in Web Origins, since it never makes a direct auth request — it just issues an HTTP redirect at the edge.

So the earlier checklist was right as written — `now.were.cooking` for `APP_BASE_URL` and Web Origins, both domains for Logout URLs.

Good news on the technical question: **no, you don't need real Auth0 access at all** for local dev, regardless of who holds the tenant credentials. Look at `src/lib/auth0.ts:9`:

```ts
export const authDisabled = process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' && !process.env.AUTH0_DOMAIN;
```

If `AUTH0_DOMAIN` isn't set locally, the app auto-logs you in as a fake "Demo cook" user (`current-user.ts`'s `DEV_USER`) and skips Auth0 entirely — `src/proxy.ts` even short-circuits the middleware when this is on. So you can hit `/today`, `/recipes`, `/pantry`, anything behind login, without your friend's Auth0 dashboard access. (Your real `.env` currently has `AUTH0_DOMAIN` set, so you'd need to comment it out locally to flip this on — just don't commit that.)

One thing worth flagging though: I pulled up this repo's own team-assignment docs (`hang.md`, `johnny.md`, `jerry.md`) to check, and "what happens after login" — `/today` and `/onboarding` — are explicitly **Johnny's** owned files (Workstream B), while your area (Workstream C) is `src/features/recipes/**`, `src/app/(app)/recipes/**`, `src/app/api/{recipes,cook}/**`. The team rule in those docs is "only edit files you own, ask in chat before touching anyone else's." So technically you can build/test those pages, but if you mean actually implementing their content, that'd be worth a heads-up to Johnny first rather than me just diving in.

So: what specifically did you want to move on to — your own recipes/cook work, or did you want help on the `/today`/`/onboarding` stubs themselves?
